Abstract.AbstractText: Unique nanoporous Co3O4 fibres and sheets were successfully fabricated via a facile hydrothermal route (150 °C) and subsequent annealing process at 500 °C in air. The excellent microwave absorption of the nanoporous Co3O4 materials originates not only from the dielectric loss and impedance matching, but also from geometrical effects. Herein, the photocatalytic behavior of the as-prepared Co3O4 has also been reported based on the degradation of methylene blue (MB) dye in an aqueous medium under simulated solar light.
